record.paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
record.original_question: Given a finite digraph D and a positive integer k, if the minimum out-degree of D is at least 2k - 1, must D contain k pairwise vertex-disjoint directed cycles?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.3 Let D be a digraph and k ∈ Z>0. If δ +(D) ≥ 2k − 1 then D contains k vertex-disjoint cycles.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D=(V,A)$ be a finite directed graph (loops and multiple arcs forbidden) and let $k$ be a positive integer. The minimum out-degree of $D$ is $\delta^{+}(D) := \min_{v \in V} |\{u \in V : (v,u) \in A\}|$. A directed cycle is a sequence $v_1 v_2 \cdots v_\ell v_1$ of distinct vertices ($\ell \geq 2$) such that $(v_i,v_{i+1}) \in A$ for each $i$ (indices mod $\ell$). Two directed cycles are vertex-disjoint if they share no vertex. 

Prove or disprove: for every positive integer $k$ and every finite digraph $D$ with $\delta^{+}(D) \geq 2k-1$, $D$ contains $k$ pairwise vertex-disjoint directed cycles.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is confirmed for $k=1$ (trivial), $k=2$ (Thomassen, 1983), and $k=3$ (Lichiardopol, Pór, Sereni). It has also been verified for tournaments (Bang-Jensen, Bessy, Thomassé) and for digraphs with minimum semi-degree $\geq 2k-1$ in special classes, but the full conjecture remains open for general digraphs when $k \geq 4$.

status_evidence.title: The Bermond-Thomassen Conjecture | Open Problem Garden
status_evidence.snippet: Bermond and Thomassen conjectured that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least 2k-1 contains k disjoint cycles; verified for k=2 and k=3, open in general.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is still open for k ≥ 4 in general digraphs.

status_evidence.title: A Step toward the Bermond–Thomassen Conjecture about Disjoint Cycles in Digraphs
status_evidence.snippet: Proof that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least 5 contains three disjoint cycles, establishing the k=3 case.

status_evidence.title: Disjoint 3-Cycles in Tournaments: A Proof of the Bermond-Thomassen Conjecture for Tournaments
status_evidence.snippet: The Bermond-Thomassen conjecture is proved for tournaments.

status_evidence.title: Two disjoint cycles in digraphs
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the k=2 case originally settled by Thomassen.
